title: Frobenius and separable factors of a nonconstant smooth proper curve map
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C,D$ be smooth proper geometrically integral curves of dimension one over $k$ [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $u:C\to D$ be a nonconstant $k$-morphism, where nonconstant means not factoring through a $k$-rational point of $D$. There exist a smooth proper geometrically integral $k$-curve $C'$ of dimension one and $k$-morphisms $F:C\to C'$ and $v:C'\to D$ with $u=v\circ F$, such that $v$ is nonconstant and its induced extension of function fields $k(C')/k(D)$ is finite separable [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower]. The factorization can be chosen as follows.

If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, take $C'=C$, $F=\operatorname{id}_C$, and $v=u$. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that
$$C'=C^{(p^n)}:=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,\,\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)}\operatorname{Spec}k,\qquad \varphi_n:k\to k,\quad a\mapsto a^{p^n},$$
with the $k$-structure on $C'$ given by the second projection [def-pc-base-change], [def-pc-field-characteristic]. Here $F$ is the $n$-fold relative Frobenius: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C$ its ring map is $A\otimes_{k,\varphi_n}k\to A$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a^{p^n}b$.

The characteristic-zero case is the identity factorization, with separability as in fields.tex Tag 030K (fields-lemma-separable-first).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms] to $u$. Write $K=k(D)$ and $L=k(C)$ and regard $K$ as a subfield of $L$ by $u^*$. The cited statement gives that $L/K$ is finite, that both fields are finitely generated of transcendence degree one over $k$, and that morphisms of these smooth proper integral curves are determined by their induced field embeddings.

source.place: Tag 0CD2 (curves-proposition-unwind-morphism-smooth), first sentence of proof, using Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], the separable algebraic closure $E$ of $K$ in $L$ is a subfield with $E/K$ separable algebraic and $L/E$ purely inseparable. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, the same cited statement says $E=L$. Thus $L/K$ is finite separable. In this case $C'=C$, $F=\operatorname{id}_C$, and $v=u$ give all the assertions. Henceforth assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$.

Apply [lem-sfb-curve-intermediate-field-realization] to $u$ and $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$. It gives finite $E/K$ and $L/E$, a smooth proper integral curve $Z$, a $k$-isomorphism $\theta:k(Z)\cong E$, and nonconstant maps $a:C\to Z$, $b:Z\to D$ with $u=b\circ a$ and the prescribed field embeddings. Thus the extension induced by $a$ is finite purely inseparable, while that induced by $b$ is finite separable, by step 2 and these identifications.

source.place: Tag 0CD2 (curves-proposition-unwind-morphism-smooth), proof, the sentence realizing the intermediate field as X -> Z -> Y; Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), equivalence of (1) and (6); Tag 0BY3 (curves-lemma-nonsingular-model-smooth), smoothness over a perfect field.

proof.text: The map $a$ has smooth proper integral dimension-one source and target and finite purely inseparable function-field extension. Thus [lem-sfb-purely-inseparable-curve-frobenius] gives $n\geq0$ and a $k$-isomorphism $h:C^{(p^n)}\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ with $a=h\circ F_{C/k,n}$. Set $C'=C^{(p^n)}$, $F=F_{C/k,n}$, and $v=b\circ h$. Then $v\circ F=b\circ a=u$. Since $h$ is a $k$-isomorphism, $C'$ is smooth proper integral of dimension one, $v$ is nonconstant, and $k(C')/v^*K$ is isomorphic to $k(Z)/b^*K$, hence finite separable.

Apply [lem-sfb-frobenius-twist-geometric-integrality-affine] to the geometrically integral $C$, in characteristic $p$ and at the integer $n$ of step 4. It gives geometric integrality of $C^{(p^n)}$, its second-projection $k$-structure, and exactly the displayed affine formula for $F_{C/k,n}$, including $n=0$. Together with step 4 this supplies every remaining clause.
